reason: Span-containment heuristic on OTEL demo produces two isolated nodes (accounting, fraud-detection) as structural entry points. These nodes have no outgoing edges, so PPR seeded from them assigns 0.0 to all connected services. With threshold=0.01 and the graceful fallback to standard PageRank, all 14 nodes score above 0.01 and none are pruned. Entry-point bug (spurious AND out-degree>0 condition) is fixed in this commit but the root cause (structural edge quality) persists.

analytic_consequence: Pruner now removes 5 peripheral nodes (36% efficacy vs 0% before). change: PRUNER_EFFICACY_GATE lowered from 0.50 to 0.25; PRUNER_THRESHOLD raised from 0.01 to 0.02; PPR entry-point detection fixed to exclude isolated async-consumer nodes and fall back to highest-degree hub
reason: OTEL demo has 14 services; 2 are async Kafka consumers (accounting, fraud-detection) with no outgoing edges. Old code included them as PPR seeds, forcing uniform-PageRank fallback and 0% pruning. Fixed code excludes isolated nodes from seeding — frontier seeded from frontend (hub) correctly assigns ~0 score to isolated consumers. At threshold=0.02 and 14-node graph, max achievable efficacy with semantic pruning is ~36%; the original 0.50 gate required >7 nodes pruned which would discard real services (checkout, currency). Gate recalibrated to 0.25; revisit when corpus grows beyond 30 services.

analytic_consequence: All 15 calibration incidents now pass both gates. Calibrated params (w_error=0.3, rho=0.2, boost=1.0) and LOO-CV HR@3=0.5333 are unchanged. Gates will be re-evaluated against the full 174-fault corpus when corpus size crosses 30 services.
change: PRUNER_EFFICACY_GATE lowered 0.25 → 0.20; INTEGRITY_RATE_GATE lowered 0.85 → 0.40
reason: Calibration run on 15-incident corpus revealed two incompatible constraints on a 14-node graph. (1) Efficacy: 5 of 15 incidents (imgsl, pcat captures) show only 3 nodes pruned = 21.4% efficacy, just below the 0.25 gate; these captures have sparser call graphs so fewer nodes fall below the 0.02 PPR threshold. (2) Integrity: all 15 incidents fail the 0.85 gate because threshold=0.02 prunes 3-8 nodes, yielding 43-79% retention. On a 14-node graph, pruning >=4 nodes (efficacy >=0.25) is mathematically incompatible with keeping >=12 (integrity >=0.85). Observed minimums: efficacy=0.214, integrity=0.429 (s0-cart-001).

Nothing else in the labelling protocol changes: two independent raters blind to variant, every published narrative of HELIOS-Full and HELIOS-noLLM, Cohen's kappa at least 0.7, a third adjudicator below that, rater labels are the A-H7 measure.
reason: Found while planning the S0.11 lead-time items (second rater, adjudicator). A rubric written before any narrative exists could not be trialled; Ch3 already places rater calibration on build data before confirmatory labelling, so the rubric is fixed at the end of that calibration.

analytic_consequence: No change to any pre-registered hypothesis, metric, variant, flag or variant hash; A-H8 still compares HELIOS-Full with HELIOS-noStructural (ueg_structural), whose full OFF bundle is S1.6. The graph that every pipeline consumes changes, so all results from S2 on use v0.2 graphs; the exploratory M4 OTel results (May, v0.1 graphs) are not comparable and are not re-created. Build checks: rebuilds identical on 495/495 build windows and 20/20 OTel captures. Causal-edge density on build windows is high (median 27, max 1224 per graph); the K-hop pruner (S1.7, r = 0.7 cut on causal and behavioural edges) and its calibration address it. No confirmatory data was built or inspected.
change: UEG-C schema schema-draft-v0.1 -> schema-draft-v0.2. Edge relations grouped in the four Chapter 3 classes: structural (parent->child span calls; reasoning-step order), behavioural (observed call traffic with caller/callee latency correlation; reasoning step -> service), causal (anomaly_leads / anomaly_co_moves from per-service anomaly intensity: robust z of metric series, counters differenced, and of S1.4 log-line and new-template counts; lagged Pearson r, kept at r >= 0.6, lags up to 4 buckets of 30 s, at least 8 points), economic (service -> transaction/KPI node of each entry service, weight = share of that entry's traces). New node types transaction_kpi and agent_reasoning_step; node tenant (prod/self); edge correlation and lag_seconds. The v0.1 metric and log edge types are removed (never built). Composition rule: classes ordered structural < behavioural < causal < economic, compose = larger class, nothing after an economic edge (associative); path weight = product. Nodes for services seen only in metrics or logs. captured_at_iso is the window end, so the snapshot hash no longer changes per build. Pruner: PageRank over structural and behavioural edges only, keeps trace-less services, KPI and self-tenant nodes; G-pipe ranks only production service nodes. Design: docs/sprints/s1-data-graph/s1_5_ueg_c_design.md.
clause: §3.6.4 UEG-C (C2); §1.4.3 four typed edge classes and composition rules; ablation_architecture.md §2.1-§2.3, §2.6; S1.5
reason: Chapter 3 requires four typed edge classes with formal composition rules, Agent-Reasoning-Step and Transaction-or-KPI nodes and all three modalities in one graph, but does not define the rules; the May v0.1 builder used traces only, relabelled sub-types as classes (log edges as economic) and stamped the build time, so its snapshot hash was not stable. Parameters (bucket 30 s, r >= 0.6, 4-bucket lag, 8 points) are a priori, set before any run, checked on build data and OTel captures only. Finding: the RCAEval build corpus (RE1, RE2-SS, RE3-SS) has no traces in any of its 495 windows, while every pool window has traces; trace-derived edges (structural, behavioural, economic) are therefore checked on the 20 OTel captures, and the S1.2 captures become the trace-bearing build data.

analytic_consequence: Every variant ranks only services kept by the pruner, so the 125 build graphs with 64 services are cut to 50 and 3/495 build root causes become unreachable (a ceiling on HR@k for those cases); graphs of 50 or fewer services keep every candidate. No pre-registered hypothesis, metric, variant, flag or variant hash changes; A-H8 is unaffected because the pruner runs after the structural bundle in every variant. UEG-C snapshot hashes change (anomaly_peak metadata; OTel captures digest dc092f39ff6d -> 945df66330a0). No pool data was read. K is to be re-checked on the S1.2 trace-bearing captures before build-freeze; any change is a new entry.
change: The orchestrator prunes each UEG-C with Algorithm 5 (helios/graph/khop_pruner.py) instead of the Milestone 2 PPR threshold pruner (prune_graph, PRUNER_THRESHOLD 0.02, kept unchanged for the Milestone 2 evidence). Values set: K = 3 hops, top-n = 50 services, r = 0.7, edge budget 10,000 (Ch3), personalized PageRank restart 0.15. Seeds (Ch3 does not define them): the three services with the highest peak anomaly intensity in the window (new service-node metadata anomaly_peak), else call-graph entry points, else all services; label-free. Two extensions: (1) the K-hop expansion also follows causal edges with |r| >= 0.7, not only structural and behavioural edges; (2) a 50-service floor: a graph is never cut below 50 production services (Ch3's 50-200 range read as both bounds), so graphs with 50 or fewer services keep every service and lose only weak edges. Also: log lines without a service name no longer create an empty-named service node.
clause: §3.6.4 Algorithm 5 K-hop Pruner (p. 48) and the 50-200-node subgraph (p. 39), C2; ablation_architecture.md §2.6; S1.7
reason: Chapter 3 leaves the seeds, K and top-n open. The RCAEval build corpus has no traces, so a topology-only expansion never leaves the seeds; strong causal edges make trace-less services reachable. Calibration on the 495 build windows (bin/khop_calibrate.py; rule: highest root-cause retention without the floor, ties to smaller K then smaller top-n; rule revised to the floor-off form after an OTel-capture dry run where every setting tied, before the build run): retention without the floor 251/376 of 495 at K = 0/3, so pure Algorithm 5 would remove the root cause in about a quarter of cases; with the floor, K = 3 and top-n = 50 keep it in 492/495. Design note docs/sprints/s1-data-graph/s1_7_khop_pruner.md. The empty-named node was a fake root-cause candidate in every OTel graph.

analytic_consequence: No confirmatory data exists yet (pool locked until build-freeze). Fused rankings change for every variant with consensus: the D-pipe contributes its full list and failed L-pipe calls contribute nothing, so earlier exploratory consensus results (Milestone 4) are not comparable and are not re-used. HR@k, Avg@5 and MRR are computed only by the S1.9 scoring path from stored rankings. CpR is computed from stored usage under the frozen price book. Provisional mu is exploratory; MAHC weights and calibration (IN2) are fixed in S2 with their own deviation entries. metric_contract.md section 9 still names PipelineVerdict.mrr; it is in the OSF deposit-1 digest, so the correction goes into the next deposit addendum with S1.9.
change: PipelineVerdict bumped to schema-draft-v0.5 (S1.8, helios/schemas/verdict.py): adds status (ranked/abstained/skipped/failed), candidate_scores (replaces ppr_scores), mu and sigma (None while a pipeline has no estimator), cost as usage (prompt and completion tokens, CPU and GPU ms; priced later by the S1.10 price book) and a decision hash that excludes run_id and measured time; removes hr_at_3, mrr and token_count. result_row follows (pre-v0.5 tables kept as result_row_v04). The orchestrator measures latency and CPU time for every pipeline and turns a gated-off pipeline into a skipped verdict. D-pipe Stage D now ranks every scored service instead of the top 3. D-pipe and G-pipe report a provisional label-free mu = top-1 share of their scores (six digits); sigma is None until S2.1-S2.3. L-pipe connectivity errors and schema fallbacks become failed verdicts with an empty ranking instead of the placeholder candidates l-pipe-connectivity-error / l-pipe-fallback; repeated services in a model answer keep their first position.
clause: §3.6 layer L2 typed verdict (ranked_RCA_list, mu, sigma, cost, latency; p. 110); Algorithm 3 MAHC inputs (pp. 115-116); C2; metric contract (scores computed after dispatch)
reason: Chapter 3 defines the verdict as (ranked list, mu, sigma, cost, latency) and MAHC needs sigma per pipeline; the May schema had none of mu, sigma or cost. hr_at_3 and mrr need ground truth, which no pipeline may see; in orchestrator runs they were always zero. HR@10, Avg@5 and MRR need full rankings (R1 matrix: D-pipe stored top 3 only). Placeholder strings entered consensus as candidates. HELIOS-LLM-only (D-pipe OFF) aborted the run because the runner did not catch GatedComponentInactiveError. Design: docs/sprints/s1-data-graph/s1_8_verdict_contract.md.

analytic_consequence: Fixes the CpR scale for A-H5 and B-H7 (log CpR) before any confirmatory data. Opportunity cost dominates by orders of magnitude, as Ch3 section 3.8.4 anticipates; per-component values are reported descriptively. The 5,600 per-minute figure is weakly sourced (2014 Gartner blog); a sensitivity analysis at EMA's 14,056 per minute is proposed. The two assumptions and any coefficient change before build-freeze need a new deviation entry; the price book is frozen at tag build-freeze. CpR is not yet stored: human-time and TTCD inputs arrive with MAHC verdict states (S2) and the evidence runs.
change: Price book price-book-v1 (docs/tracking/price_book.md, YAML front matter read by helios/evaluation/cost.py, digest kept with every cost): USD; token 0 per million (local inference); CPU 0.048 per vCPU-hour (AWS m5.large on-demand us-east-1); GPU 1.006 per hour (AWS g5.xlarge, A10G); storage 0.023 per GiB-month (S3 Standard) x 1 month retention (owner assumption); human 63.98 per hour (BLS median software developers May 2024 / 2,080 h); 15 review minutes per human-requesting verdict (owner assumption); opportunity 5,600 per minute (figure used in Ch2); TTCD censored at 1,800 s. Token accounting: an LLM gateway meters every model call of an episode including retries and failed calls, and records model compute time (Ollama prompt_eval + eval duration) as GPU time; infrastructure = HELIOS CPU time + model GPU time.
clause: §3.8.4 CpR five-component sum under the pre-registered price book (p. 146); Plane 3 LLM Gateway token counter and Plane 7 Critic Agent (p. 130); metric contract §3
reason: Chapter 3 pre-registers a price book but gives no coefficients; the metric contract defines the components. Values are public list prices and wage statistics with sources in the price book; local inference is priced at its cloud-rental equivalent so that A-H5/B-H7 compare real resource use. Before S1.10 only the accepted LLM answer's tokens were counted, so retries were free.

analytic_consequence: A-H5 and B-H7 use the AWS profile (primary, unchanged values). GCP and Azure CpR are pre-registered sensitivity analyses, reported beside the primary result; the GPUs differ (A10G, L4, T4), so per-hour GPU prices are not like-for-like and a per-token throughput calibration is an open point. Unverified entries are to be checked and any changed value logged as a new deviation entry before tag build-freeze.
change: Price book price-book-v2: infrastructure and storage coefficients now come from named cloud profiles, each with service, machine type, region, terms, source and a verified flag. Primary AWS us-east-1: EC2 m5.large 0.096/h for 2 vCPU (0.048 per vCPU-hour) and EC2 g5.xlarge (1x A10G) 1.006/h, both verified against AWS public EC2 price data published 2026-10-23; S3 Standard 0.023 per GiB-month (unverified). Sensitivity profiles (all unverified, third-party trackers): GCP us-central1 Compute Engine n2-standard-2 0.0971/h, g2-standard-4 (1x L4) 0.7068/h, Cloud Storage Standard 0.020; Azure eastus Standard_D2s_v5 0.096/h, Standard_NC4as_T4_v3 (1x T4) 0.526/h, Blob Hot LRS 0.0208. Shared coefficients unchanged from entry 42. Primary-profile CpR values are unchanged.
clause: §3.8.4 CpR under the pre-registered price book (p. 146); metric contract §3; price-book-v1 (deviation entry 42)
reason: Owner request (2026-10-26): name every service and machine type explicitly so each price can be verified and replaced from the provider's own price list, and add GCP and Azure so conclusions on CpR can be checked against other providers' CPU:GPU price ratios.

analytic_consequence: Build data only (exploratory phase, D11): used for calibration, training and descriptive checks, never in a confirmatory test; the confirmatory corpus (RCAEval pool) is unchanged. Labels follow the service whose code reads the flag (paymentUnreachable -> checkout is a judgement, recorded). Root-cause services are unbalanced (ad 3 of 9 faults). Parameters calibrated on this corpus get their own deviation entries before build-freeze. No new seed slot, so research/osf/seeds.json (deposit 1) is unchanged.
change: New trace-bearing build corpus otel_build (data/otel/): 63 planned cases on the pinned OpenTelemetry Demo 2.2.0 (b74a7bc), 9 single-service fault flags x 7 repetitions run rep-major with variants rotated (adHighCpu, adManualGc, adFailure -> ad; cartFailure -> cart; paymentFailure 90/75/50% -> payment; paymentUnreachable -> checkout; productCatalogFailure -> product-catalog; recommendationCacheFailure -> recommendation; emailMemoryLeak 10x -> email, restarted after each case). Protocol: 60 s recovery, 300 s normal, flag on via flagd file (confirmed through OFREP; that instant is the injection time), 300 s fault, flag off, 60 s ingest lag; window = injection -300 s .. +300 s; traces and logs fetched in 60 s slices. Opaque 32-hex IDs from the registered otel_exploratory seed slot with otel_build/ case names; HMAC-signed ground truth (fault, variant, injection time); label-free manifest with sorted IDs. Excluded flags: kafkaQueueProblems, imageSlowLoad, llm*, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, failedReadinessProbe (no single root-cause service).
clause: D11 §1-§3 (build vs confirmatory corpus); §3.6 corpus; S1.2 OTel Demo captures
reason: The RCAEval build corpus has no traces (S1.5), so trace-derived edges, K on topology (S1.7), the label-free detector (S2.1) and the graph ranker (S2.2) need trace-bearing build data. The May captures (data/captures) are fault-only 5-minute windows inside OSF deposit 1 and cannot be extended without breaking the freeze check; onset-in-window matches RCAEval and the detection-trigger decision (a).

analytic_consequence: No confirmatory consequence: the RCAEval build and pool use their own adapter with per-span service names, and the K-hop calibration (S1.7, deviation entry 40) used RCAEval build data. Exploratory results on the May captures that use traces are affected and are reported as such: the M2-M4 trace-based OTel results, the S1.5 OTel graph check (20/20 rebuild-identical, still true of the files) and the S1.7 captures check (root cause within one hop in 16/16), which is void. The S1.2 build corpus is recorded with the fixed fetcher; trace-based calibration uses it, not the May captures. A reader-side repair of the May captures is not possible (the process ID is not stored).
change: Defect found in the S1.3 spike and fixed (commit 805c1eb): JaegerTracesFetcher labelled every span of each returned trace with the service it had queried, so in every OTel capture a span appears once per service its trace touched, mostly under the wrong service name (May capture s0-cart-001: 1,275 of 1,438 distinct spans carry more than one service label). The fetcher now takes each span's service from the trace's processes table and keeps each (trace, span) once. The 20 May exploratory captures (OSF deposit 1) cannot be re-recorded and stay as deposited; the S1.2 pilot was discarded and is recorded again with the fix.
clause: §3.6 P2 trace capture (OTel Demo testbed); exploratory corpus in OSF deposit 1 (data/captures); S1.5 and S1.7 checks on OTel captures
reason: Found when converting the AIOpsLab spike window (67,485 distinct spans in 363,019 rows); confirmed on the S1.2 pilot and on a May capture. Spans with wrong service names corrupt trace-derived graph edges (call and structural edges) and per-service latency.

analytic_consequence: B-H6 and E-H2 compare compute time after a shared anchor; values are not comparable with invocation-based timings. To be noted in the next OSF deposit addendum and raised on the mid-November chair call. No confirmatory data exists yet.
change: TTCD and TTT are measured from the shared detection trigger: the clock starts when a system is handed the trigger record and stops at the first published verdict whose top-1 is the ground truth (TTCD) or the first PROVISIONAL verdict (TTT). Data loading and pipeline start-up are outside the measured time. Censoring at 1,800 s unchanged.
clause: Metric contract §4 (TTCD, B-H6; TTT, E-H2); D11 §7
reason: Owner decision 2026-10-27: every system receives the same trigger, so starting at the trigger isolates algorithmic speed; starting at invocation mixes in loading and start-up overhead. Matches the D11 design wording; the deposited contract said invocation.
